subject: DI03000141

intro_text.en: Diagram-first notes: identify parts, understand construction, follow working and practise only the syllabus numericals.
intro_text.gu: પહેલાં labelled diagram, પછી parts, Construction અને step-by-step Working. Syllabus પ્રમાણે જ numericals.

h.en: 4.1.1 Why drives are used and how to select them

body.en:
A drive transfers mechanical power between shafts while providing required speed ratio, direction, spacing and torque. Belts and friction wheels rely on friction; chains and gears use positive engagement. Rope drives suit large distances or lifting arrangements depending on rope type.

Select by power, input/output speed, centre distance, alignment, allowable slip, service factor, environment, maintenance and guarding. Belt drives are economical and absorb shocks but may slip; chains have no ordinary belt slip but need lubrication; gears give compact accurate ratios but require precise manufacture and support.
body.gu:
Drive shafts વચ્ચે power transfer કરી speed ratio,direction,spacing અને torque આપે. Belts/friction wheels friction-based; chains/gears positive engagement. Rope type પ્રમાણે long-distance અથવા lifting ઉપયોગ.

Power,speed,centre distance,alignment,slip,service factor,environment,maintenance અને guarding મુજબ પસંદ કરો. Belt economical/shock absorb; chain no ordinary belt slip પણ lubrication જોઈએ; gears compact/accurate પરંતુ precision જરૂરી.

title.en: 4.2 Belt drives: construction, working and numericals
title.gu: 4.2 Belt Drives: Construction, Working અને Numericals

h.en: 4.2.1 Flat belt, V-belt, materials and layouts
h.gu: 4.2.1 Flat Belt, V-belt, Materials અને Layouts

body.en:
Flat belt construction: a flexible strip runs over pulleys on supported shafts. Friction at the wrap transfers power through a tight/slack tension difference. Common constructions include leather historically, rubberised fabric and modern polymer/composite belts; choose a rated material for heat, oil and speed.

Open belts give the same shaft rotation direction; crossed belts reverse it but add rubbing and bending concerns. V-belts wedge into matching grooves, giving compact drives and increased frictional grip. They must contact the groove sides rather than bottom out. Match profile and length; never lever a belt onto a running pulley.
body.gu:
Flat belt flexible strip supported pulleys પર ચાલે; wrap friction tight/slack tension difference થી power આપે. Leather historically, rubberised fabric અને polymer/composites વપરાય; heat/oil/speed rating જુઓ.

Open belt same direction; crossed opposite direction પણ rubbing/bending concerns. V-belt groove sides પર wedge થઈ grip વધારે; groove bottom પર બેસવું નહિ. Profile/length match કરો અને running pulley પર belt ન ચઢાવો.

body.en:
Without slip and using consistent effective pulley diameters, N2/N1=D1/D2. Slip is relative sliding because frictional grip is insufficient. If fractional slips s1,s2 occur at the two pulleys, N2/N1=(D1/D2)(1−s1)(1−s2). Convert percentages to fractions before substitution.

Creep is small relative movement from elastic stretching on the tight side and contraction on the slack side; it is not merely gross slipping. Flat-belt thickness may affect effective diameter; V-belt calculations use pitch/effective diameters, not arbitrary outside diameters. Belts labelled synchronous/toothed use positive engagement and need a different assumption set.
body.gu:
No slip પર N2/N1=D1/D2, effective diameters consistent લો. Slip grip insufficient થી relative sliding. Fractional s1,s2 માટે ratio=(D1/D2)(1−s1)(1−s2); percent ને fraction કરો.

Creep tight-side stretch/slack-side contraction ને કારણે નાનું relative movement; gross slip જેવું નહિ. Flat thickness effective diameter બદલે; V-belt pitch diameter લો. Synchronous toothed belt positive drive હોવાથી assumptions અલગ.

h.en: 4.2.3 Angle of lap and belt-length formulas
h.gu: 4.2.3 Angle of Lap અને Belt Length

body.en:
Let larger diameter D, smaller d and centre distance C, all in the same units. Open-belt small-pulley lap theta=pi−2 asin((D−d)/(2C)); the larger pulley has pi+2 asin((D−d)/(2C)). Crossed-belt lap on each pulley is pi+2 asin((D+d)/(2C)), when geometrically feasible.

Approximate lengths for C large relative to diameter differences/sums: Lopen=2C+(pi/2)(D+d)+(D−d)²/(4C); Lcross=2C+(pi/2)(D+d)+(D+d)²/(4C). These are approximations, not exact arbitrary-spacing formulas. Use radians for the friction exponent; smaller-pulley lap commonly limits the open-belt drive.
body.gu:
D=મોટો diameter,d=નાનો,C=centre distance. Open small-pulley lap theta=pi−2asin((D−d)/(2C)); large lap plus sign. Crossed માટે બંને lap=pi+2asin((D+d)/(2C)), feasible geometry હોય ત્યારે.

Approx lengths: open 2C+pi(D+d)/2+(D−d)²/(4C); crossed માં last term (D+d)²/(4C). Large C માટે approximation છે. Friction exponent માં angle radians લો; open small pulley સામાન્ય રીતે limiting.

h.gu: 4.2.4 Solved Belt Geometry અને Speed Example

body.en:
Open belt: D=.40 m,d=.20 m,C=1.0 m. Small lap=pi−2asin(.10)=2.941 rad=168.52°. Approximate length=2+.94248+.01=2.95248 m.

If the .20 m driver rotates at1000 rpm, the .40 m follower rotates at500 rpm without slip. With2% slip at the driver only, N2=500×.98=490 rpm. Belt speed based on the driver without slip is v=pi d N/60=10.472 m/s. Clearly state which pulley drives; interchanging driver and follower inverts the ratio.
body.gu:
Open belt D.40m,d.20m,C1m: small lap=pi−2asin(.10)=2.941rad=168.52°. Approx length=2+.94248+.01=2.95248m.

.20m driver1000rpm હોય તો .40m follower500rpm no-slip. Driver slip2% હોય તો490rpm. Driver no-slip belt speed v=pi dN/60=10.472m/s. Driver કોણ છે તે સ્પષ્ટ; interchange કરતાં ratio invert થાય.

body.en:
Define T1 and T2 as TOTAL running tight/slack tensions, and Tc=m v² with m=belt mass per metre. For a flat belt, (T1−Tc)/(T2−Tc)=exp(mu theta). Useful power P=(T1−T2)v. If centrifugal effects are negligible, T1/T2=exp(mu theta).

For a V-belt with included groove angle2alpha, replace mu by mu/sin(alpha) in the ideal wedge model. Many books instead name only the effective tractive tensions T1,T2 and then write Tmax=T1+Tc. Both conventions work, but do not mix them or subtract Tc twice. Under the simple mean-elastic-tension model initial tension T0≈(TOTAL T1+TOTAL T2)/2; neglecting Tc reduces to the familiar average.
body.gu:
અહીં T1,T2 TOTAL running tensions; Tc=m v², m kg/m. Flat belt: (T1−Tc)/(T2−Tc)=exp(mu theta), P=(T1−T2)v. Tc negligible હોય તો ratio T1/T2.

V-belt included angle2alpha હોય તો ideal wedge model માં mu/sin(alpha). કેટલાક books T1,T2 effective tractive tensions કહે અને Tmax=T1+Tc લખે. Conventions mix/subtract twice નહિ. Simple mean-elastic model માં initial T0≈TOTAL tensions ની average.

body.en:
Given flat belt v=10 m/s,m=.5 kg/m,TOTAL tight limit600 N,mu=.30,lap=pi rad. Tc=.5×10²=50 N; ratio exp(.30pi)=2.566. TOTAL slack tension=50+(600−50)/2.566=264.31 N. P=(600−264.31)×10=3356.9 W≈3.36 kW. Simple-model T0≈432.15 N.

For fixed allowable total tension Tmax and other ideal conditions, maximum power occurs when Tc=Tmax/3. Thus vopt=sqrt(Tmax/(3m))=sqrt(600/1.5)=20 m/s. Do not claim the real belt can safely run at this speed without checking manufacturer speed, fatigue and pulley-size limits.
body.gu:
v10m/s,m.5kg/m,TOTAL tight limit600N,mu.30,lap pi: Tc50N, ratio2.566. TOTAL slack=50+550/2.566=264.31N. P3356.9W≈3.36kW; simple T0≈432.15N.

Ideal maximum power પર Tc=Tmax/3; vopt=sqrt(Tmax/(3m))=20m/s. Actual rated speed/fatigue/pulley-size checks વગર આ speed safe છે એવો દાવો નહિ.

h.en: 4.3.1 Rope drives: fibre and steel-wire construction

body.en:
Fibre ropes run in grooved pulleys and can transmit power over longer centre distances; several parallel ropes may be used. Steel-wire rope consists of wires twisted into strands laid around a core. Hoists, cranes and elevators use suitably designed wire ropes with sheaves/drums and terminations.

Steel ropes offer high strength and flexibility but need suitable sheave diameter, corrosion control and inspection for broken wires, wear and crushing. Rope drives are not interchangeable with arbitrary belts or lifting ropes. Never determine safe lifting capacity from rope diameter alone; use certified system ratings and inspection criteria.
body.gu:
Fibre rope grooved pulleys માં longer distances પર power આપે; multiple ropes શક્ય. Steel-wire rope માં wires → strands → core આસપાસ lay હોય. Hoists/cranes/elevators માં proper sheaves,drums,terminations સાથે વપરાય.

Strength/flexibility લાભ, પણ sheave diameter,corrosion અને broken wires/wear/crushing inspection જરૂરી. Rope diameter એકલું safe lifting rating નથી; certified system limits અનુસરો.

body.en:
Construction: roller chain links articulate on pins/bushes; rollers engage matching sprocket teeth. Working: successive tooth engagement pulls the chain and transmits motion without ordinary friction-belt slip. Polygonal action still causes speed fluctuation, especially with few teeth.

Selection steps: determine power/speed and service factor; choose standard pitch/type and number of strands from a rated catalog; choose tooth counts for required ratio and acceptable minimum teeth; check centre distance, chain length, wrap, lubrication and tension adjustment. Small pitch and adequate tooth count generally smooth operation. Positive engagement does not remove elongation, wear or the need for guarding.
body.gu:
Construction: pins/bushes પર links articulate થાય; rollers matching sprocket teeth engage કરે. Working: successive engagement થી chain ખેંચાય અને belt જેવી friction slip વગર motion મળે. ઓછા teeth પર polygonal speed fluctuation થાય.

Power,speed,service factor → rated pitch/type/strands → tooth counts/ratio → centre distance,length,wrap,lubrication,tension adjustment check કરો. Positive engagement છતાં wear/elongation/guarding જરૂરી.

body.en:
Parallel shafts use spur or helical gears; intersecting shafts often use bevel gears; non-parallel non-intersecting shafts can use worm/worm-wheel or suitable crossed-helical gears. Rack-and-pinion converts rotation to straight translation.

Spur teeth are straight and simple but can be noisy at speed. Helical teeth engage progressively and create axial thrust. Bevel teeth lie on pitch cones to change shaft direction. A worm resembles a screw driving a wheel, giving large reduction; self-locking depends on lead angle, friction and operating conditions, not merely its name. Select by torque, ratio, speed, shaft arrangement, efficiency and bearing loads.
body.gu:
Parallel shafts: spur/helical; intersecting: bevel; nonparallel nonintersecting: worm અથવા suitable crossed-helical. Rack-pinion rotation ને linear travel આપે.

Spur simple પણ speed પર noise; helical gradual engagement સાથે axial thrust. Bevel pitch cones shaft direction બદલે. Worm screw-like driver large reduction આપે; self-locking lead angle/friction/conditions પર આધારિત, દરેક worm self-locking નથી. Torque,ratio,speed,shaft layout,efficiency,bearing loads મુજબ selection.

h.en: 4.4.2 Gear nomenclature and the meshing condition

body.en:
Pitch circle is the reference rolling circle; pitch diameter d=mZ with module m and tooth count Z. Circular pitch p=pi m. Addendum extends from pitch circle to tooth tip, dedendum to root; clearance permits tooth-tip space. Backlash is circumferential tooth-space clearance, not centre distance. Pressure angle defines the line-of-action direction.

Meshing involute spur gears require compatible module and pressure angle. For standard external gears at standard centre distance, C=(d1+d2)/2. The illustrated concentric circles label tooth-height references only; actual involute tooth flanks are not drawn.
body.gu:
Pitch circle reference rolling circle; d=mZ, p=pi m. Addendum pitch થી tip, dedendum root તરફ; clearance tooth-tip space. Backlash circumferential tooth-space clearance છે, centre distance નહિ. Pressure angle line-of-action direction આપે.

Involute spur gears mesh કરવા compatible module/pressure angle જોઈએ. Standard centre distance C=(d1+d2)/2. Diagram tooth-height reference circles છે; actual involute flanks નથી.

h.en: 4.4.3 Simple gear train: speed ratio and train value
h.gu: 4.4.3 Simple Gear Train: Speed Ratio અને Train Value

body.en:
Define speed ratio i=Ninput/Noutput and train value TV=Noutput/Ninput=1/i; state this convention because some texts reverse the names. For an external pair, N2/N1=Z1/Z2 in magnitude and the rotations are opposite.

In a simple train each shaft has one gear. Intermediate idlers change output direction and spacing but cancel from the overall speed magnitude. Example A20T drives B30T drives C60T, with NA=600 rpm: NB=400 rpm opposite A; NC=200 rpm same direction as A. Overall i=3, TV=1/3.
body.gu:
અહીં i=Ninput/Noutput; TV=Noutput/Ninput=1/i. Books માં naming બદલાય એટલે convention લખો. External pair N2/N1=Z1/Z2 અને directions opposite.

Simple train માં એક shaft પર એક gear. Idlers ratio magnitude માં cancel થાય પણ direction/spacing બદલે. A20T→B30T→C60T, NA600rpm: NB400 opposite, NC200 same as A; i3,TV1/3.

body.en:
Construction: at least one shaft carries two gears rigidly keyed together in different axial planes. They rotate at the same speed, though their tooth counts differ.

Example: A20T drives B40T; B shares a shaft with C20T; C drives D60T. At NA=1200 rpm, NB=NC=600 rpm and ND=200 rpm. Speed ratio=(40/20)(60/20)=6; train value1/6. With two external meshes, D rotates in the same direction as A. Multiply stage ratios, not all driving/driven tooth counts indiscriminately; shared-shaft gears are not meshing with each other.
body.gu:
Construction: ઓછામાં ઓછા એક shaft પર બે gears rigidly keyed, અલગ axial planes માં. Teeth અલગ પણ speed same.

A20→B40; B shaft પર C20; C→D60. NA1200rpm તો NB=NC600, ND200rpm. i=(40/20)(60/20)=6,TV1/6. બે external meshes હોવાથી output same direction. Shared-shaft gears એકબીજા સાથે mesh નથી થતા.

body.en:
A reverted train is a compound train with input and output axes coincident. The syllabus table says “Riveted”; the standard gear-train term used here is reverted, also supported by the listed gear-train laboratory content.

For A driving B and coaxial C driving D, equal module requires ZA+ZB=ZC+ZD to obtain the same centre distance. Example20+52=28+44=72. Overall speed ratio=(52/20)(44/28)=4.0857; with input1000 rpm output244.76 rpm. If modules differ, equate m1(ZA+ZB)=m2(ZC+ZD), not tooth sums alone. Epicyclic numerical analysis is excluded by this syllabus.
body.gu:
Reverted train compound train છે જેમાં input/output axes coincide. Syllabus table માં “Riveted” છે; standard term reverted અહીં વપરાયો છે.

A→B અને B સાથે coaxial C→D માટે equal module હોય તો ZA+ZB=ZC+ZD. Example20+52=28+44=72. i=(52/20)(44/28)=4.0857, input1000rpm → output244.76rpm. Modules અલગ હોય તો m1 sums=m2 sums. Epicyclic numericals syllabus માં excluded છે.

q.en: Which drive relies on positive engagement?
Open-belt shaft directions?
What is creep?

a.en: Relative movement caused by changing elastic belt strain.
a.gu: Elastic belt strain બદલાવથી relative movement.

q.en: What unit is used for lap in exp(mu theta)?
What is centrifugal tension?

a.en: Tc=m v² with m in kg per metre.

q.en: Ideal maximum-power condition?
Why V-grooves?

a.en: Wedging increases normal contact force and grip.
a.gu: Wedging થી contact normal અને grip વધે.

q.en: Can wire-rope capacity come from diameter alone?

a.en: No; construction, grade, terminations and certified system ratings matter.

q.en: What is module?

a.en: Pitch diameter divided by tooth count.

q.en: Does an idler change simple-train speed magnitude?

a.en: No, but it affects direction and shaft spacing.

q.en: What is a reverted train?

a.en: A compound train with coaxial input and output.

q.en: Are all worm drives self-locking?

a.en: No; it depends on geometry, friction and operation.
